title: Drift Wood #2 · the vending machine
logline: A dollar goes in. Nothing comes out. Wood takes it personally, then philosophically.

panels.composition: The cafeteria's vending machine. WOOD feeding a dollar into it with the care of a man defusing something.

characters.pose: feeding a bill into a vending machine

image.prompt: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized wool overcoat carefully feeding a limp dollar bill into a school vending machine, harsh fluorescent light

panels.composition: The machine's coil turns. The bag of chips hangs, caught.

image.prompt: close-up inside a vending machine window, the metal coil turned and a bag of chips hanging caught on the edge, not falling

panels.composition: Wood, forehead against the glass. A STUDENT passing behind him.

characters.pose: forehead against the glass, hands flat on it

balloons.text: This machine has taken my dollar and given me a lesson about desire. That is not what I asked for.

image.prompt: a teenage boy pressing his forehead and both hands against the glass of a vending machine while a student passes behind him

panels.composition: The student, now gone, has left. Wood alone, still at the glass. In the reflection, the bag of chips and his own face, both hanging.

balloons.text: Fine. Keep it. I'll write about you.

image.prompt: a teenage boy alone at a vending machine, his face reflected in the glass beside a hanging bag of chips, empty cafeteria behind, heavy black spotting

notes: The strip learns its own move: a small indignity, a large sentence, a smaller one.
